title: Addressing and the Hop-by-Hop Journey of a Message

reasons: Appeared in the supplied midterm (Q3c, 4 marks) using exactly the slide figure (A/10 … P/95)
Tests understanding of physical vs logical addresses

intro.why: The midterm’s 4-mark trace question uses this figure exactly. You must say which addresses change at every hop and which stay the same.
objectives: Name the four levels of addresses in TCP/IP
Explain hop-to-hop (data link) vs source-to-destination (network) delivery
Trace a frame from Host A to Host D through two routers, showing addresses at every hop

explain.bn: TCP/IP এ চার ধরনের অ্যাড্রেস: **physical (link)**, **logical (IP/network)**, **port**, এবং **specific** অ্যাড্রেস। Physical অ্যাড্রেস ডেটা লিংক লেয়ারে (যেমন ৬-বাইট MAC: 07:01:02:01:2C:4B), logical অ্যাড্রেস নেটওয়ার্ক লেয়ারে, port অ্যাড্রেস ট্রান্সপোর্ট লেয়ারে (কোন প্রসেস), আর specific অ্যাড্রেস অ্যাপ্লিকেশনে (ইমেইল, URL)।

ডেটা লিংক লেয়ার ফ্রেমকে **এক হপ (node) থেকে পরের হপে** নেয় — তাই physical অ্যাড্রেস প্রতি হপে বদলায়। নেটওয়ার্ক লেয়ার প্যাকেটকে **source host থেকে destination host পর্যন্ত** নেয় — তাই logical অ্যাড্রেস সাধারণত একই থাকে। ট্রান্সপোর্ট লেয়ার **process-to-process** ডেলিভারি করে — port অ্যাড্রেসও একই থাকে।

চিত্রে “A/10” মানে **logical address A, physical address 10**। Router 1 এর দুই ইন্টারফেস: LAN 1 এর দিকে F/20, LAN 2 এর দিকে T/99। Router 2: LAN 2 এর দিকে N/33, LAN 3 এর দিকে Z/66। Host D: P/95। ফ্রেমের ফরম্যাট (স্লাইডের চিত্র): **[destination physical | source physical | A P | Data | T2]** — প্রথমে গন্তব্যের physical, তারপর উৎসের physical, তারপর logical source A ও destination P, শেষে trailer T2।

রাউটার ফ্রেম পেয়ে ডেটা লিংক হেডার/ট্রেইলার খুলে ফেলে (**decapsulation**), নেটওয়ার্ক লেয়ারে destination logical address (P) দেখে কোন দিকে পাঠাবে ঠিক করে (**routing**), তারপর পরের লিংকের জন্য **নতুন physical source ও destination** দিয়ে নতুন ফ্রেম বানায় (**encapsulation**)। logical A→P অপরিবর্তিত থাকে।

slideDefs.text: Four levels of addresses in TCP/IP protocols: Physical (link), logical (IP, network), port, and specific addresses.
The data link layer is responsible for moving frames from one hop (node) to the next.
The network layer is responsible for the delivery of packets from the source host to the destination host.
The physical addresses will change from hop to hop, but the logical addresses usually remain the same.
The physical addresses change from hop to hop, but the logical and port addresses usually remain the same.

solved.title: Trace A/10 → P/95 (midterm Q3c)
solved.rule: Physical changes per hop; logical (and port) stay the same.
calc: Hop 1 (LAN 1): Host A → Router 1 — frame [20 | 10 | A P | Data | T2]
At Router 1: decapsulate, read P, route to LAN 2, re-encapsulate
Hop 2 (LAN 2): Router 1 → Router 2 — frame [33 | 99 | A P | Data | T2]
At Router 2: decapsulate, route to LAN 3, re-encapsulate
Hop 3 (LAN 3): Router 2 → Host D — frame [95 | 66 | A P | Data | T2]
At Host D: frame accepted (95 matches), decapsulated up to the upper layers
solved.bn: প্রতিটি LAN এ শুধু সেই LAN এর দুই প্রান্তের physical address থাকে।

examAnswers.question: Consider the network in Figure 1. A message is sent from host A to host D through the intermediate routers. Trace the journey of the message across each hop and analyze how the message fields change at every stage of transmission.
examAnswers.answer:
Notation: logical/physical (e.g. A/10). Frame = [destination physical | source physical | A P | Data | T2].
1. Host A builds a packet with source logical address A and destination logical address P. Since P is on another network, the frame is sent to Router 1 on LAN 1: [20 | 10 | A P | Data | T2].
2. Router 1 (F/20) accepts the frame, removes the data-link header and trailer, checks the destination logical address P and forwards the packet to LAN 2. It creates a new frame: [33 | 99 | A P | Data | T2].
3. Router 2 (N/33) repeats the process and forwards on LAN 3: [95 | 66 | A P | Data | T2].
4. Host D (P/95) accepts the frame because 95 is its physical address and passes the data to the upper layers.
Analysis: the physical (link) addresses change at every hop because the data link layer delivers hop-to-hop, while the logical addresses A and P (and port addresses) remain the same because the network layer delivers from source host to destination host.

mistakes.m: Changing logical addresses A and P at each router.
mistakes.fix: Logical addresses usually stay the same end to end; only physical addresses change.

mistakes.m: Writing the router’s logical address (F, T) inside the frame.
mistakes.fix: Router interfaces’ physical addresses (20, 99, 33, 66) appear in frames; the packet keeps A and P.
Slide frame shows destination physical first, then source (e.g. 20 10).

mistakes.m: Using Router 2’s LAN 3 interface (66) on LAN 2.
mistakes.fix: On LAN 2 the destination is Router 2’s LAN 2 interface — read the figure carefully.

takeaways: Four address levels: physical, logical, port, specific.
Data link: hop-to-hop; network: source-to-destination; transport: process-to-process.
Physical addresses change at every hop.
Logical and port addresses usually remain the same.
Frame on each LAN uses the physical addresses of that LAN’s two ends.

recall.q: Which address changes at every hop?

flags.text: In the photographed exam figure the labels of Router 2 are partly unclear. Forouzan’s Figure 2.18 (the slide source) uses Router 2 = N/33 on the LAN 2 side and Z/66 on the LAN 3 side, giving the frames 33 99 and 95 66. Follow your printed paper if it differs.
